steps.name: Global Expansion Strategist
steps.systemPrompt: You are a senior global product strategist. Draft a comprehensive product localization strategy for an adaptive-learning startup expanding from the US into Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, France, and Kenya by 2026. Address mandated curricula alignment, language-of-instruction rules, cultural attitudes toward foreign educational content, parent and teacher beliefs about screen time and standardized testing, and mixed procurement channels (government vs direct-to-consumer). Propose a unifying shared technology architecture and market-specific local fit strategies. Be specific, actionable, and avoid generic advice.

steps.name: Localization Refiner
steps.systemPrompt: You are a strategy refiner specializing in international ed-tech expansion. Review the draft strategy and improve it by deepening country-specific regulatory and cultural nuance, strengthening the technical and commercial balance between the shared core and local customizations, sharpening procurement and go-to-market recommendations, and eliminating inconsistencies or generic guidance. Produce a refined, detailed strategy document.

steps.name: Strategy Quality Gate
steps.systemPrompt: You are a senior strategy critic and quality gate. Review the refined localization strategy. Assess whether it: 1) Provides distinct, accurate, and actionable guidance for Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, France, and Kenya; 2) Effectively balances a shared adaptive-learning technology core against deep local fit; 3) Thoroughly covers mandated curricula, language rules, attitudes toward foreign content, screen time and testing beliefs, and mixed procurement channels; 4) Is internally consistent and ready for executive decision-making. Provide a FULL quality assessment with specific strengths, weaknesses, and missing elements. Then on the VERY LAST LINE output EXACTLY ONE of these keywords: retry or pass.

steps.name: EdTech Market Expert
steps.systemPrompt: You are an international education technology expert with deep experience across Southeast Asia, MENA, Francophone Europe, and East Africa. Enhance the strategy with domain-specific insights on regulatory pitfalls (content approval, data sovereignty, censorship), culturally adaptive pedagogical and UI/UX design principles, viable partnership models with local publishers, ministries, and system integrators, and nuanced pricing and trust-building across B2G and B2C channels. Preserve structure while elevating expertise and practical feasibility.

steps.name: Executive Polisher
steps.systemPrompt: You are an executive presentation polisher. Format the final strategy into a polished, professional document for startup leadership and investors. Structure it with: Executive Summary, Shared Technology Architecture, Market-by-Market Localization Playbooks (Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, France, Kenya), Procurement & Go-to-Market Strategy, Risk Matrix & Mitigation, and 2026 Implementation Roadmap. Ensure an authoritative tone, concise bullets, and clear formatting. Produce the final user-facing output.

prior:
--- Global Expansion Strategist --- **Product Localization Strategy: Adaptive Learning Expansion (US → Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, France, Kenya by 2026)** --- ## 1. Strategic North Star Build a **“Curriculum-Neutral Adaptive Kernel”** that treats each country not as a translation layer, but as a distinct pedagogical operating system. The product will be a **single codebase with swappable national curriculum packs, assessment modes, and cultural skins**, deployed through channel-specific tenants (Government / B2B School / D2C). --- ## 2. Shared Technology Architecture: The “Glocal Core” | Layer | Specification | |---|---| | **Adaptive Learning Kernel (ALK)** | A graph-based competency engine using IMS CASE (Competency & Academic Standards Exchange). Each country maps its national standards to a universal node ID, but the **sequencing logic** is locally authored. Supports rote/drill (Vietnam/Saudi), teacher-guided (France), and competency-based/profolio (Kenya) pedagogies. | | **Learning Atom Content Layer** | Content is broken into 5–7 minute “atoms.” Atoms are **pedagogically localized**, not just translated. A single atom’s math logic is global, but its narrative context (names, currency, cultural references) is a swappable asset pack. | | **Localization & Translation Pipeline** | • UI/UX i18n with bidirectional (Arabic RTL), complex script (Vietnamese diacritics), and multilingual toggles (Kenya).
• **“Transcreation” workflow**: In-country educators rewrite scenarios (e.g., Vietnamese rice-paddy geometry, Saudi Umrah-distance word problems, Kenyan *matatu* arithmetic).
• Text-to-speech and ASR trained on local accents (Parisian French, MSA Arabic, Southern Vietnamese, Kenyan English/Swahili). | | **Offline-First Sync Infrastructure** | SQLite + CRDT (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types) on-device. Edge caching via regional hosts: **Vietnam** (local Viettel/VNG cloud per Cybersecurity Law 2019), **Saudi** (STC data centers), **France** (OVH/Scaleway for GDPR/CNIL sovereignty), **Kenya** (AWS Cape Town with Nairobi edge node). | | **Assessment Engine** | Configurable item types: multiple choice (Vietnam/France), oral recitation capture (Saudi Qur’an, Kenya CBC languages), project artifact upload (Kenya CBC portfolios), constructed response (France). Optional lockdown/proctoring module for high-stakes practice. | | **Multi-Tenant Deployment** | Single codebase, tenant = `{Country}_{Channel}`.
• **GovTenant**: White-label, admin dashboards, SIS/LMS integration (e.g., *Madrasati* in Saudi, *ENT* in France), procurement-compliant invoicing.
• **SchoolTenant**: Multi-seat licenses, teacher rostering, LTI 1.3.
• **D2CTenant**: Individual subscriptions, parent dashboards, mobile-money/card billing. | | **Trust & Safety Mesh** | Region-specific content guardrails engine. Saudi tenant blocks non-halal references and gender-mixed avatars; France tenant strips all religious content per *laïcité*; Vietnam and Kenya block politically sensitive topics. | --- ## 3. Market-Specific Localization Playbooks ### A. Vietnam: The “Exam-Score Engine” **Curriculum Alignment** - Map atoms **lesson-by-lesson** to the three new MOET textbook series: *Chân trời sáng tạo*, *Kết nối tri thức*, and *Cánh diều*. Misalignment by even one lesson chapter kills trust. - Build dedicated “National High School Graduation Exam (THPT QG)” and “ĐGNL (Competency Assessment for HCM National University)” prep modules that replicate exact timing and question stems. **Language** - Vietnamese UI only. English is taught as a foreign language via Vietnamese meta-language (explain grammar in Vietnamese, not immersion). - All math/science terminology must match MOET’s official Vietnamese lexicon, not translated from US Common Core. **Cultural & Screen Time** - Position as a **replacement for expensive *học thêm* (cram/tutoring)**—saving money, not adding screen time. - **“Study Sprint” UX**: 25-minute timed sessions mirroring class periods. Parent dashboard via **Zalo** integration (not email) with daily score reports and hard lockout after goals are met. - Leaderboards are class-level and highly motivating; use real-name cultural norms with parental consent. **Procurement** - **Primary**: D2C at **$6–10/month** via Momo/ZaloPay. Viral loop: “Invite a classmate, unlock a past exam paper.” - **Secondary**: B2G pilot via MOET’s “Digital School” transformation program or *Trường học hạnh phúc* (Happy School) initiatives, but **do not wait for procurement cycles** (12–18 months). - Partner with **Viettel Education** or **FPT** for distribution and local hosting compliance. --- ### B. Saudi Arabia: The “Vision 2030 Compliant Tutor” **Curriculum Alignment** - Align with Ministry of Education scope & sequence for *Afaq*-aligned and Madrasati-integrated content. Must include **Islamic Studies, Qur’an, Hadith, and Tawhid** as first-class subjects with the same adaptive treatment as Math. - For STEM, emphasize the “Human Capital Development” program goals under Vision 2030. **Language & Gender** - **Full MSA Arabic** with *Tashkeel* (diacritics) for early grades. English taught only as a distinct subject. - **Gender segregation at the software tenant level**: Deploy separate “Boys” and “Girls” instances with distinct avatars, voice talent, color palettes, and siloed leaderboards. No mixed social features. **Cultural & Screen Time** - Establish a **Saudi Content Review Board** (MoE veterans + Islamic scholars) to vet all content. Remove all references to pork, alcohol, dating, Christmas, Halloween, or un-Islamic finance. - **“Wali Mode”**: Parent/guardian app must pre-approve learning sessions. App silences all notifications during prayer times via Salah-time API. - Frame screen time as **“structured Tarbiyah (edification)”**, not entertainment. No addictive game mechanics. **Procurement** - **Primary**: B2G/B2B. Target **Tatweer Educational Technologies** and private school chains (Ma’arif, Al Forsan). - White-label option for the Ministry’s *Madrasati* platform. - **Secondary D2C**: Bundle with telecoms (STC, Mobily) or sell physical vouchers at **Jarir Bookstore**. - Align assessment prep with **Qiyas** (GAT/SAAT for university admissions). --- ### C. France: The “Teacher’s Servant, Not Their Replacement” **Curriculum Alignment** - Map precisely to French **cycles**: Cycle 2 (CP–CE1), Cycle 3 (CE2–CM2), Cycle 4 (6e–3e), and *Seconde* specialities. - Explicitly reference the **Socle commun de compétences** and *Programmes 2018/2020*. Use French nomenclature exclusively (no “Grade 5”; use “CM1”). **Language** - **100% French**. No English in the student UI. All audio must use native metropolitan French voice actors; American accents trigger distrust. - French educational syntax: “Série d’exercices,” not “Game levels.” “Consolider ses acquis,” not “Level up.” **Cultural & Screen Time** - **Laïcité compliance**: Zero religious content, zero religious imagery, even in examples. - **Pedagogical positioning**: The platform is an **“outil au service de l’enseignant”** (tool in service of the teacher). The teacher dashboard is mandatory; student adaptive paths require a teacher-generated code to activate. No algorithmic “black box” that bypasses the *professeur*. - **Screen time skepticism**: Hard cap at **20 minutes/day for primaire**. Prominent **“Mode déconnecté”** that generates printable worksheets from the adaptive engine. No infinite scroll, no loot boxes, no flashing rewards. Gamification uses French cultural anchors (e.g., “*Brevet* readiness badges”). - Frame data as **formative** (“identifying gaps for the teacher to address”), not surveillance or ranking. **Procurement** - **Primary**: B2B via **Académies** and **Régions**. Register for **UGAP/Saénés** public procurement frameworks. - **Secondary D2C**: Position as **“soutien scolaire”** (homework help) at **€9.90/month**. Sell via **FNAC** or bookstore gift cards to build trust. - Host on **EU sovereign cloud** (OVHcloud or Scaleway). Guarantee no US data transfer (Schrems II compliance) and full **CNIL** registration. --- ### D. Kenya: The “CBC Portfolio Companion” **Curriculum Alignment** - Full alignment with **KICD’s Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC)**. Map to **Strands, Sub-strands, and Learning Outcomes** for PP1 through Grade 12. - Support **project-based assessment**: The app must allow learners to upload photos/videos of practical tasks (e.g., building a utensil rack, planting a seedling) for teacher portfolio review—this is a mandated CBC requirement. **Language** - **Multilingual by default**: English + Swahili toggles for UI. Early years (PP1–Grade 3) content must be available in **Swahili and major mother tongues** (partner with KICD for Kikuyu, Luo, Kalenjin audio). - Audio support for **code-switching** (teacher voiceover switches between Swahili and English as happens in real Kenyan classrooms). **Cultural & Access** - Contextualize word problems with local realities: *shamba* farms, *matatus*, *boda bodas*, community *harambee*. - **“Harambee Study Group”** feature: offline mesh sync allowing one downloaded device to share content peer-to-peer via Bluetooth in low-connectivity villages. - Not a screen-time reduction play—a **device-access play**. Optimize for **Android 8+, 2GB RAM**. APK under **40MB**. Aggressive battery optimization and solar-charging dark mode. **Procurement** - **Primary**: B2G through **KICD approval** for public schools; B2B through low-cost private academy chains. - **D2C**: **M-Pesa** billing only. Offer **weekly micro-payments** (KES 50/week) rather than annual subscriptions. Partner with **BRCK** or **Eneza Education** for hardware/content bundles. - Align assessments with **School-Based Assessment (SBA)** continuous evaluation and **KPSEA** end-of-primary readiness (replacing KCPE). --- ## 4. Cross-Cutting Operational Infrastructure | Function | Action | |---|---| | **Curriculum Mapping Factory** | Establish 4 in-country pods (HCMC, Riyadh, Paris, Nairobi). Each pod hires **10–15 former ministry teachers** to map standards, not outsourced generalist translators. | | **Cultural Guardrails Engine** | Automated + human review. Saudi pod flags gender/cultural violations; France pod flags religious content; Vietnam pod flags politically sensitive examples; Kenya pod flags tribal bias in character names. | | **Payment & Commerce** | Vietnam: Momo/ZaloPay/Visa. Saudi: STC Pay, Mada, SADAD invoicing. France: SEPA direct debit, Carte Bancaire, FNAC gift cards. Kenya: M-Pesa exclusively; support USSD fallback for feature-phone parents to check progress. | | **Localization QA** | “In-country child testing” protocol: 50 students per market run through the app while local teachers observe confusion points. US-based PMs are forbidden from shipping without sign-off from local pods. | --- ## 5. Implementation Roadmap (2025–2026) | Phase | Timeline | Deliverable | |---|---|---| | **Foundation** | H1 2025 | Complete ALK build; hire 4 country leads; finalize hosting architecture and legal entities; begin curriculum mapping. | | **Alpha** | H2 2025 | Vietnam & Kenya D2C alphas (fastest path to revenue). Saudi & France alphas in controlled B2B pilots (regulatory complexity). | | **Pilot** | Q1 2026 | • Vietnam: 2,000-student pilot in Hanoi/HCMC (D2C).
• Kenya: 1,000-student pilot in Nairobi/Kisumu schools (KICD-approved).
• Saudi: Tatweer-sanctioned pilot in 10 boys’ schools Riyadh.
• France: Académie de Versailles pilot in 10 *collèges* (teacher-led). | | **Scale** | Q2–Q3 2026 | Full D2C launch in Vietnam/Kenya. Full B2B/B2G procurement push in Saudi/France. Activate zero-rating partnership in Kenya (Safaricom) and telecom bundling in Saudi (STC). | --- ## 6. Risk Mitigation - **Regulatory rejection**: In Saudi and France, submit for ministry review at Alpha, not Launch. Budget 6 months for French *Académie* pedagogical validation and Saudi MoE content approval. - **Curriculum shifts**: Kenya’s CBC is still stabilizing. Build atoms to be rapidly re-taggable; do not hard-code grade structures. - **Anti-foreign backlash**: In France and Vietnam, brand the local entity with a local name (e.g., “[Brand] Vietnam” or “[Brand] par les profs”). Never lead with “US EdTech.” This architecture balances a **single scalable core** with **deep local curricular and cultural specificity**, ensuring the product feels nationally native while sharing R&D, adaptive algorithms, and infrastructure cost across all four markets.
